properties.name: Stream Opening: Bjerkedalen Park
properties.description: Water shapes the landscape and is something everyone can relate to. Water is a unifying and formative element that recurs in all urban planning, landscape architecture, and garden design. Norway has 82,000 rivers and streams. Every valley has a river, and every small ravine has a stream. This gives the Norwegian and Nordic landscape a constant sense of freshness. Because streams connect vast distances while taking up little space, we have the opportunity to develop a distinctly Norwegian or Nordic park style along these waterways. These narrow parks become biological corridors in the landscape, and together with the accompanying walking paths, they represent Norway’s contribution to a modern park policy. The daylighting of the Hovinbekken stream was a key reason why Oslo and its waterway policy were recognized as part of Oslo’s designation as European Green Capital in 2019.

properties.name: Reopening of Hovinbekken at Jordal
properties.description: When Hovinbekken was reopened through Ensjø, it laid the foundation for reopening the stream further downstream at Jordal. The project was coordinated with the development of the new Jordal Amfi and Jordal Sports Park, allowing the stream solution to be integrated into the overall area. The open stream adds a distinct landscape element with trickling water and lush vegetation, giving the area a more natural and vibrant character. At the same time, emphasis has been placed on stormwater management: the stream is designed to retain and delay both stream water and rainwater from surrounding areas. The stream at Jordal was reopened in autumn 2020.

properties.name: Reopening of Hovinbekken from Hasle to Ensjø Torg
properties.description: The reopening of Hovinbekken from Hasle to Ensjø Torg has been carried out step by step since 2012, and the work continues in one of the most densely populated areas in the country. The project began with the planning of Ensjø, aiming to transform the area from a ”car city to a housing city”. The reopening includes, among other elements, the park and water treatment facility Teglverksdammen, and extends through Ensjø to Ensjø Torg. The project has also paved the way for reopening Hovinbekken at Jordal and Klosterenga. The reopening at Hasle and Ensjø was awarded the Oslo City Architecture Prize in 2023, and is part of the effort to facilitate movement through nature - from the forest to the fjord.
